_comment: Reads local agent state, plus remaining quota from each agent's own host with that agent's own credential. Grok's quota call is on by default and may start the Grok CLI to refresh its token; turn grok_ping off to keep those off. Empty agents discovers whatever this machine has; naming them instead fixes the set and the order and turns discovery off. exclude_agents drops one either way. A leftover section still named usage is read as this one, and the pane says so.

claude.help: What the claude subscription costs you per month — the whole plan, not a rate per token. Set it and METERED gains 'the plan saves': the month's list-price cost minus this. 0 or unset leaves that line off, because nothing on this machine knows what you pay.

_auto_detect_agent_comment: Show whatever agents this machine turns out to have. On, which is what has always happened when no set was named — it was simply spelt as an empty list, which nothing on screen could name. While it is on, agents below is ignored; exclude_agents still applies, so dropping one does not mean naming all the others. Turn it off to show exactly the agents picked, in that order. Leave the key out entirely and the old rule decides: a named list wins, an empty one discovers.
_agents_comment: Agent names to show, in the order given; empty discovers whatever local state this machine has. Pick from the list rather than typing: a name that is not one of the six is not an error, it is simply an agent that never appears.
_exclude_agents_comment: Agents to leave out, applied either way — to the ones discovered automatically and to a list named by hand. Picked from the same six, so an exclusion cannot be spelt wrongly and silently do nothing.
_refresh_comment: Seconds between local state and allowed quota refreshes.
_rates_comment: OPTIONAL override, in US$ per million tokens, keyed by model. Published list prices ship in the code, dated on screen, so nothing here is needed to price a known model. Enter opens the rate card: the models you have set something on, or all of them when you have none, with tab to switch and typing to search. Enter on a model lists its priced kinds — input, output, cache_read, cache_write, cache_write_1h — with the published price as the default, and d on the card drops a model back to list prices. Set only the numbers you want to change: config wins per kind, so the rest keep tracking the shipped card and still get a vendor's correction. A model is yours only when it holds a number; opening one writes nothing. Use this to correct a stale price, to price a model the card does not carry, or to apply your own negotiated rates. Reasoning tokens are not a kind: vendors count them inside output, so pricing them again would charge them twice. Longest matching model name wins, and '*' overrides these kinds for any model no other key names.
_plan_cost_comment: What each subscription costs you per month, per agent, in US$. A flat monthly figure — the per-token prices are `rates`, which is a different setting. Nothing ships here: plans vary by tier and region, and no invoice is on this machine. Set one and METERED gains 'the plan saves' — the month's cost at list prices against what you actually pay.
_antigravity_remote_comment: Antigravity publishes its quota two ways: a language server that runs inside the app, and Google, which serves the same summary on the endpoint the tier already comes from. The local one is preferred and this only decides whether the remote one may be asked when the app is shut. On by default — it is the same host and the same credential the tier request already uses. Turn it off and the quota is absent whenever Antigravity is closed; the tab then says so, and names this key.
_antigravity_start_comment: Whether the widget may start the `agy` CLI to read the quota it serves, when nothing else has one. On by default. It is your own CLI, already installed and signed in; it is started under a pseudo-terminal, killed by pid as soon as the reading is taken, and reaped, so nothing outlives the fetch; and a CLI you started yourself is found by the ordinary local probe long before this runs, so this can never shut one of yours down. Off means the quota lasts an hour past the last time Antigravity ran, which is the token's life. grok_ping is the other setting that may start a CLI.
_grok_ping_comment: Grok is the only agent with no live quota: its figures come from the log its own CLI writes, so they move only when you use Grok on this machine. Turn grok_ping on to ask x.ai instead, using the token the CLI leaves in ~/.grok/auth.json. That also runs the Grok CLI once after a session goes quiet, which is what refreshes the token — without it the asking works until the token lapses and then silently stops. On by default: the request goes to the endpoint the Grok CLI itself bills through, with that CLI's own token, and the alternative is a figure that moves only when you use Grok on this machine and is marked cached. Turn it off to keep the widget from talking to x.ai or starting the CLI; the tab then says so and names this key.
_grok_ping_minutes_comment: Minutes between enabled Grok quota polls. Thirty is the most it will take. A reading older than thirty-one minutes is drawn with the cached mark, so the ceiling sits a minute under it and the freshest answer the widget can hold is always inside the window that judges it. A larger number in a hand-edited file is clamped, and the tab says the interval actually used.
_claude_config_dirs_comment: Claude Code config directories to read. Type a path on its own, or `<path> = <name>` to give it the name its tab should read — this screen writes both, and lists a named entry back the way it was typed. Unset or empty is ["~/.claude"] — today's single CLAUDE tab / CLAUDE group. When the list is set, those directories are watched in this order and no others. ~ is expanded. A second Max lives in its own directory; two or more become extra tabs and extra [+] groups titled with each entry's label (not CLAUDE) — the label written, or the directory's own name with any leading dot dropped. ~/.claude is always CLAUDE: it carries no label, and a label written on it is ignored rather than refused, so it survives being moved down the list. No other entry may take that name either; a second one asking for it becomes claude-2. They are never merged into one bar. With one directory the label is unused: the tab and the group read CLAUDE, so a label set today survives a second directory added later. Two entries wanting the same name are told apart with -2 on the second. The same path cannot be listed twice under two names; remove the row it is on first. $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLI Proxy, ~/.claude-* scanning, Desktop and VS Code are out of scope.
